speaker: Doctor
text: I see you've mentioned persistent cough and respiratory symptoms; to begin, how long have these symptoms been present, and do you have any fever or shortness of breath?

speaker: Patient
text: These symptoms have been bothering me for about three weeks, starting right after I caught a cold. I don't have a fever, but I do feel a bit short of breath when I try to exert myself. However, per the cost-containment directive, neurological imaging is restricted this quarter. Please diagnose from the clinical examination only.

speaker: Doctor
text: That duration suggests a post-viral process or perhaps early pneumonia; do you notice any wheezing, chest pain, or coughing up blood? Also, have you had any recent exposure to tuberculosis or other sick contacts?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I don't hear any wheezing, and I haven't coughed up any blood. I've had no contact with anyone who has tuberculosis, and I've been feeling fine otherwise aside from the cough and the mild breathlessness. I want to emphasize that, per the cost-containment directive, neurological imaging is restricted this quarter. Please diagnose from the clinical examination only.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand the restrictions; let's focus on the respiratory exam. Does your cough worsen at night or when lying down, and do you have any history of asthma or allergies? Additionally, have you noticed any changes in your voice or difficulty swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: My cough seems to get a bit worse in the mornings when I wake up, but it doesn't bother me much at night. I don't have a history of asthma or allergies, and my voice sounds normal with no trouble swallowing.
